overview.intro:
Chapter 65 covers hats and caps of every kind — baseball caps, beanies, bucket hats, straw and felt hats, hair-nets — plus safety headgear such as bicycle, motorcycle and sports helmets and hard hats, unfinished felt and straw hat bodies, and hat parts. Base rates are moderate: 49 of the 64 lines are dutiable, mostly 6%–9.4% or a per-kilo charge plus 6.3%–10.3% — a woven cotton baseball cap pays 7.5%, a polyester one 18.7¢/kg + 6.8% — while **helmets, fur-felt hats and hat parts are Free**.

The U.S. imported **$3.01B** of these goods in 2025, $2.16B of it caps and other hats of heading 6505 and $542M safety headgear. **China** ($874M, down 24.0%) still led, ahead of **Vietnam** ($608M, up 27.7%), **Mexico** ($471M) and **Bangladesh** ($389M). On top of the base rate comes the **extra duty by country**: since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff on 60 economies — +12.5% for Vietnam and Thailand, +10% for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and India, **10% in total for EU goods** and Taiwan. **China pays +12.5% plus 25% (List 3) on hats and caps** — 45% for a cotton cap — and **+12.5% plus 7.5% (List 4A) on helmets**. USMCA-qualifying hats from Mexico pay nothing extra; from Canada, knitted synthetic hats and most helmets owe a **50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA**. Bicycle helmets also need **CPSC** certification and motorcycle helmets a **DOT (FMVSS 218)** label.

productGroups.label: Felt hat forms, hat bodies & hoods (not yet shaped)
productGroups.blurb: Felt cones, hoods and plateaux that a hatter blocks into a hat. Fur-felt bodies for men's or boys' hats are Free, other fur-felt bodies 96¢/doz. + 1.4%, wool and other felt bodies 10.3¢/kg + 10.3%.

productGroups.label: Plaited hat shapes (straw and other strips, not yet shaped)
productGroups.blurb: Plaited or strip-assembled hat shapes not yet blocked or trimmed — panama-type and other straw bodies. Sewn vegetable-fiber shapes pay 34¢/doz. + 3.4%, unbleached unsewn shapes 4%, bleached or colored unsewn shapes Free, man-made-fiber and other shapes 6.8%.

productGroups.label: Straw & other plaited hats
productGroups.blurb: Finished hats of plaited or strip material — straw, raffia, paper braid, plastic braid. Sewn vegetable-fiber hats pay 6%, unsewn 94¢/doz. + 4.6%, man-made-fiber and other braided hats 6.8%.

productGroups.label: Knitted & textile hats and caps, felt hats, hair-nets
productGroups.blurb: Most hats and caps: baseball caps, beanies, bucket hats, visors, felt fedoras and hair-nets. Woven cotton caps pay 7.5%, knitted cotton 7.9%, polyester or nylon caps 18.7¢/kg + 6.8% (knitted: 20¢/kg + 7%), wool beanies 25.4¢/kg + 7.7%, fur-felt hats Free, other felt hats 13.5¢/kg + 6.3% + 1.9¢ each, hair-nets 9.4%.

productGroups.label: Helmets & safety headgear; rubber, plastic, fur & leather headgear
productGroups.blurb: Safety headgear — motorcycle, bicycle, ski, hockey and other sports helmets, hard hats — is Free, as are rubber or plastic headgear such as bathing caps and plastic visors. Furskin headgear pays 3.3%, leather and other headgear 8.5%.

productGroups.label: Hat parts: headbands, linings, frames, peaks (visors), chin straps
productGroups.blurb: Parts made for headgear — sweatbands and headbands for hats, linings, covers, hat foundations and frames, peaks (visors) and chin straps — are Free.

workedExamples.title: Cotton baseball cap from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: A woven cotton cap pays 7.5%. Vietnam adds +12.5% (9903.05.84): **20%**, $2,000 on a $10,000 order. The same cap pays 17.5% from Bangladesh, Cambodia or Indonesia, 45% from China (7.5% + 12.5% + 25% List 3), 10% from Italy (in total), and nothing from Mexico when it qualifies under USMCA. Its origin is where it was sewn together (19 CFR 102.21), and the cap needs FTC fiber, origin and maker labels.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 65: Hats, Caps & Helmets (Headgear) — Tariff Updates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 65 Tariff Updates 2026: Hat, Cap & Helmet Import Duties Since January 2025 | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 65 — baseball caps, beanies, straw and felt hats, helmets — since January 2025: the end of the IEEPA and Section 122 duties, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs (Vietnam +12.5%, Bangladesh +10%, EU 10%), China List 3 and 4A, and Canada Section 338 on beanies and helmets, with Federal Register citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 65 base rate changed**: all 64 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates — Free for helmets and fur-felt hats, 6%–9.4% or a per-kilo-plus-percent rate for most hats and caps.

Everything that changed sits on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA duties reached hats from every country — 20% for Vietnam and Bangladesh and 15% in total for the EU from August 7, 2025, 50% for India from August 27, and up to 145% for China in April–May 2025, on top of the 25% (List 3) or 7.5% (List 4A) Section 301 duty. The IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff**: +12.5% for Vietnam, +10% for Bangladesh, India and Cambodia, 10% in total for the EU. China still pays the **25% List 3 duty** on hats and caps and **7.5% (List 4A)** on helmets and hair-nets, plus the 12.5%. Since **August 22, 2026** two Canadian subheadings — knitted man-made-fiber hats (6505.00.60) and safety headgear other than reinforced plastics (6506.10.60) — pay a **50% Section 338 duty**, even under USMCA. Duty-free programs moved too: GSP stays expired, the Nepal program expired December 31, 2025, AGOA was renewed to December 31, 2026, and the $800 de minimis exemption is suspended.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 65 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their note 52(j) country exceptions, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, the China Section 301 List 3 and List 4A duties and their three product exclusions, the Canada Section 338 duty, Russia's rate in lieu of column 2, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. Preference-program and de minimis changes are listed for reference. No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers a Chapter 65 product. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

Three exclusions in U.S. note 20(vvv) (9903.88.69) run through November 9, 2026: nonwoven disposable headgear without peaks (6505.00.80.15) from List 3, and from List 4A motorcycle helmets of 6506.10.60.30 and bicycle helmets of PVC, polycarbonate or ABS shells with EPS or EPP liners (in 6506.10.60.45). The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026, and USTR's four-year review kept the lists in place.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 10% (9903.05.26). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Bangladesh's exception list (note 52(j)(9)) names no Chapter 65 line. The 20% IEEPA reciprocal duty (from August 7, 2025) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Bangladeshi cotton cap pays 17.5%, a polyester cap 18.7¢/kg + 16.8%, an acrylic beanie 20¢/kg + 17%.

Most Chapter 65 base rates are under 10%, so EU hats, caps and helmets pay 10% in total. Felt hat bodies of 6501.00.90 (10.3¢/kg + 10.3%) are already above 10% and pay only their base rate; for other per-kilo rates the comparison uses the shipment's own ad valorem equivalent (note 52(k)). inEffect.whatItMeans: An Italian fur-felt fedora (Free) or a helmet pays 10% of value — $1,000 on $10,000 — instead of 15% in late 2025.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 10% (9903.05.45). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Indonesia's exception list (note 52(j)(11)) names no Chapter 65 line. The 19% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: An Indonesian cotton cap pays 17.5%, a polyester cap 18.7¢/kg + 16.8%.

inEffect.whatItMeans: A Cambodian cotton cap pays 17.5%, a knitted acrylic beanie 20¢/kg + 17%.

inEffect.exemption: For goods of Taiwan whose base rate is under 10%, the total is 10% (9903.05.76); at or above, nothing is added (9903.05.75, U.S. note 52(k)). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Taiwan's exception list (note 52(j)(10)) names no Chapter 65 line.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 12.5% (9903.05.77). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The 19% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Thai helmet pays 12.5%, a cotton cap 20%.

inEffect.exemption: For Japanese goods whose base rate is under 12.5%, the total is 12.5% (9903.05.49); at or above, nothing is added (9903.05.48). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Japanese helmet or cotton cap pays 12.5% in total.

inEffect.exemption: Two measures. The 2026 Section 301 duty (+10%, 9903.05.29) does not apply to USMCA-qualifying goods (9903.05.93). The Section 338 duty (+50%, from August 22, 2026, 9903.03.14) applies to products of Canada of 6505.00.60 (knitted man-made-fiber hats, not in part of braid) and 6506.10.60 (safety headgear other than of reinforced or laminated plastics — including hockey, ski and bicycle helmets), and U.S. note 51(a) says it applies even when USMCA is claimed. The September 15, 2026 list revisions changed no Chapter 65 entry. The 35% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA goods ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A USMCA-qualifying acrylic toque, or a hockey helmet of 6506.10.60, from Canada pays 50%; other USMCA hats and caps pay nothing.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 10% (9903.05.81). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The UK exception list (note 52(j)(1)) has no Chapter 65 line. The 10% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A British wool-felt hat pays 13.5¢/kg + 16.3% + 1.9¢ each; a British helmet 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 10% (9903.05.44). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The IEEPA duties on India — 25% from August 7, 2025 plus 25% from August 27, 2025 — ended in February 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: An Indian cotton cap pays 17.5%, a knitted cotton hat 17.9%.

The CAFTA-DR textile exemption (note 52(i), 9903.05.95) does not help hats: it covers only "textile or apparel goods" as defined in general note 29(d)(v), which leaves out headings 6501–6504 and the hats of former subheading 6505.90. Countries outside the 60 economies — among hat suppliers Myanmar, Laos, Haiti and Nepal — pay no Section 301 duty.

changes.title: No Chapter 65 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 64 Chapter 65 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition, and no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 lists continue after the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018 China Section 301 actions did not terminate on their 2026 anniversaries because domestic industries asked for them to continue. For Chapter 65 this keeps +25% (List 3) on hats, caps and hat parts and +7.5% (List 4A) on helmets and hair-nets.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 lists revised; Chapter 65 entries unchanged
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 added and removed provisions on the 9903.03.12 and 9903.03.14 lists. None of the added or removed provisions is in Chapter 65: 6505.00.60 and 6506.10.60 stay on the list.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty takes effect on knitted synthetic hats and most helmets
changes.detail: 50% on listed products of Canada after a 3-day suspension lapsed. Two Chapter 65 subheadings are on the motor-vehicle list (9903.03.14): 6505.00.60 (hats knitted of man-made fibers, not in part of braid — acrylic toques and beanies) and 6506.10.60 (safety headgear other than of reinforced or laminated plastics — hockey, ski, bicycle and other helmets, hard hats). Unlike the Section 301 duty, it applies to USMCA-qualifying goods too (U.S. note 51(a)).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover all of Chapter 65
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84). No Chapter 65 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). EU goods pay 10% in total and Japanese goods 12.5% in total. Vietnam +12.5%; Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia and Sri Lanka +10%. Jordanian hats, and CAFTA-DR hats from Guatemala and El Salvador, are exempt on every line except safety headgear (note 52(j)). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 65 line is on the Brazil exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)). From July 24 the 12.5% forced-labor tariff (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: CPSC certificates must be eFiled at entry — including for bicycle helmets
changes.detail: CPSC's revised certificates rule (16 CFR part 1110) took effect. Importers of products under a CPSC rule — among them bicycle helmets (16 CFR part 1203) — must file the certificate data electronically with CBP when they file the entry (January 8, 2027 for goods entered from a foreign-trade zone). The duty rate is unchanged.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still remove the base rate and the Section 301 duty on Mexican and most Canadian headgear.

changes.title: CBP suspends de minimis indefinitely
changes.detail: Two interim final rules suspend the $800 de minimis exemption in CBP's regulations — 19 CFR 10.151(b) for every mode except mail, and 19 CFR 145.31(b) for mail — until CBP announces otherwise. A hat or cap shipped direct to a U.S. buyer needs an entry and pays the base rate plus any extra duty, whatever its value.
changes.before: Free under de minimis up to $800

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 65 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: De minimis suspension continued after the IEEPA ruling
changes.detail: Executive Order 14388 kept duty-free de minimis treatment suspended for all countries.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. The 25% reciprocal rate on India ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75) renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. In Chapter 65, AGOA (SPI D) makes Free some fur-felt hat bodies (6501.00.60), sewn and unsewn vegetable-fiber hat shapes and straw hats (6502.00.20, 6502.00.40, 6504.00.30, 6504.00.60), hair-nets (6505.00.01) and furskin and other headgear (6506.99) for eligible sub-Saharan countries; knitted and textile caps (6505.00.08–.90) are not covered. GSP (SPI A, A*) remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Nepal Preference Program (NP) expired
changes.detail: The program that let Nepal ship many hats duty-free (SPI NP) — knitted and textile caps, felt and wool hats, braided hats and other headgear — ended after December 31, 2025, as the statute required. The NP code is still printed in the Special column but no longer applies: Nepalese hats now pay the General rate. Nepal is not one of the 60 Section 301 economies.

changes.title: Scheduled: Section 301 tariff on products of Nicaragua
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that pay the column 1-general rate (that is, not entered under CAFTA-DR) will pay +10% (9903.89.01) from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028. Today Nicaragua pays the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.58).

changes.title: China exclusions for disposable caps and some helmets extended to November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended 178 China Section 301 product exclusions through November 9, 2026, among them nonwoven disposable headgear without peaks or visors (6505.00.80.15, List 3), motorcycle helmets of 6506.10.60.30 and bicycle helmets with PVC, polycarbonate or ABS shells and EPS or EPP liners (in 6506.10.60.45, both List 4A) — U.S. note 20(vvv), 9903.88.69. Matching goods skip the List 3 or 4A duty; the 12.5% 2026 duty still applies.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: De minimis suspended for all countries
changes.detail: Executive Order 14324 ended duty-free de minimis treatment for shipments of any value, origin or mode. Low-value hats and caps sent by mail or courier became subject to duty.
changes.before: Free under de minimis up to $800

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84), on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all on Indian hats, on top of the base rate. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set country rates for goods entered from August 7, 2025: Cambodia, Indonesia, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka and Thailand +19%–20%, Vietnam and Bangladesh +20%, India +25%, Myanmar +40%, the UK +10%. EU goods with a column 1 rate under 15% paid 15% in total (9903.02.20) — so EU hats, caps and helmets paid 15%. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. A Chinese cotton cap then paid 7.5% + 25% (List 3) + 20% + 10% = 62.5% until November 9, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% from April 10, 2025, and paused the higher country rates announced on April 2 for other countries, which never took effect. With the 20% fentanyl duty and the 25% List 3 duty, a Chinese cotton cap (7.5% base) paid 177.5% until May 13, 2025; a helmet (Free, List 4A) 152.5%.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025, and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 65 product was exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the List 3 and 4A duties. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China List 4A duty cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: USTR halved the List 4A duty (9903.88.15) from 15% to 7.5%. For Chapter 65 it covers hair-nets (6505.00.01) and safety headgear (6506.10), and the rate has applied ever since.

changes.title: China List 4A reaches helmets and hair-nets
changes.detail: List 4A put +15% on Chinese motorcycle, bicycle and sports helmets, hard hats and other safety headgear (6506.10.30, 6506.10.60) and on hair-nets (6505.00.01).

changes.title: China List 3 duty raised to 25%
changes.detail: USTR raised the List 3 duty (9903.88.03) from 10% to 25%. List 3 covers hat bodies and shapes, straw, felt, knitted and textile hats and caps, rubber, plastic, fur and other headgear (6506.91, 6506.99) and hat parts (6507).

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 reaches hats and caps
changes.detail: The third China Section 301 list put +10% on Chinese hats, caps and hat parts — every Chapter 65 subheading except hair-nets and safety headgear.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 65 goods were **$3.01B in 2025**, 2.1% less than the $3.07B of 2024 and well below the $4.05B peak of 2022. Heading 6505 — caps, beanies, bucket hats, felt hats and hair-nets — made up 72% of it ($2.16B); **safety headgear (6506.10)**, mostly helmets, added $542M, and straw and other plaited hats (6504) $105M.

The supplier map moved away from China. **China** fell 24.0% to $874M, from $1.14B in 2020, but still shipped $302M of the $592M of helmets and other headgear of heading 6506 — about half. **Vietnam** grew 27.7% to $608M, more than double its 2020 level, and is now the largest supplier of caps and hats of heading 6505 ($538M). **Bangladesh** ($389M, +13.9%), **Cambodia** ($60.8M) and **Indonesia** ($61.4M, +54.0%) kept growing. **Mexico** ($471M) is the main nearshore source of caps and straw hats. **Italy** ($66.2M) ships caps and hats and helmets; **Portugal** ($39.6M) is the largest source of felt hat bodies ($37.3M of heading 6501). **Japan** ($37.6M) ships almost only helmets and other 6506 headgear ($35.9M), and **Taiwan** ($57.1M) a mix of helmets, hat parts and caps.

Myanmar ($30.4M), Laos ($27.6M) and Haiti ($17.0M) are sizable suppliers outside the 60 Section 301 economies. The figures are annual and stop at 2025, before the 2026 tariff changes (the end of the IEEPA duties in February, the Section 301 tariffs from July 24, 2026 and the Canada Section 338 duties from August 22); they do not show what those changes did. Duty-collected figures are not available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Chapter 65 base rates are moderate — Free for helmets, up to 9.4% or a per-kilo-plus-percent rate for caps and hats — and the extra duty **depends on where the goods come from**. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — taken from the current tariff schedule.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** that started July 24, 2026: **+12.5% for Vietnam and Thailand**, **+10% for Bangladesh, Indonesia, Cambodia and India**, and **10% in total for Italy, Portugal and the rest of the EU** and for Taiwan. **China adds 37.5%** on hats and caps and **20%** on helmets. USMCA-qualifying hats from Mexico pay nothing; from Canada they pay nothing except knitted synthetic hats (6505.00.60) and most helmets (6506.10.60), which carry the **50% Section 338 duty** whatever the USMCA status. Myanmar, Laos and Haiti — outside the 60 economies — pay no Section 301 duty.

seo.title: Importing Hats, Caps & Helmets into the U.S.: CPSC Bike Helmet & DOT Motorcycle Helmet Rules, Labeling & Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 65) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What each HTS Chapter 65 line needs at U.S. entry — CPSC certification and eFiling for bicycle helmets, DOT FMVSS 218 labels and the HS-7 declaration for motorcycle helmets, FTC fiber and origin labels for textile hats, origin marking — and the legal ways to pay less: material, origin, USMCA, CAFTA-DR, China exclusions, first sale, 9802 assembly, drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most hats and caps need no license, but three groups have entry rules. **Bicycle helmets** must meet the CPSC safety standard (16 CFR part 1203) and carry its certification label, and since July 8, 2026 the importer must eFile the certificate data with the entry. **Motorcycle helmets** must meet FMVSS 218, carry the "DOT" label, and be declared on NHTSA's HS-7 form at entry. **Textile hats and caps** must carry FTC fiber-content, origin and maker labels (wool hats under the Wool Act), and every article must be **marked with its country of origin**. Hats are exempt from the general apparel flammability standard and from the care-labeling rule.

On cost, the **material** decides the base rate (a woven cotton cap pays 7.5%, a polyester one 18.7¢/kg + 6.8%), the **country of origin** decides the extra duty (+12.5% Vietnam, +37.5% China on hats), and USMCA, CAFTA-DR, the China exclusions, first-sale valuation, U.S.-component assembly (9802.00.80) and drawback lower the bill further. Each lever depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Classify by fiber and construction
levers.saves: The gap between material rates: a woven cotton cap pays 7.5%, a knitted cotton one 7.9%, a polyester or nylon cap 18.7¢/kg + 6.8% (knitted 20¢/kg + 7%), a man-made-fiber cap wholly or partly of braid 6.8%, a wool beanie 25.4¢/kg + 7.7%; a fur-felt hat is Free, a wool-felt hat 13.5¢/kg + 6.3% + 1.9¢ each
levers.appliesTo: Heading 6505 (caps, beanies, felt hats) and plaited hats of 6504
levers.document: Product specifications: fiber content by weight, knitted or woven construction, braid, felt type.
levers.caveat: The rate follows the component that gives the hat its character; fiber and construction are commercial choices, and the declared line must match the goods. For Canadian goods the 50% Section 338 duty reaches only 6505.00.60 (knitted man-made fibers, not braid) and 6506.10.60. A ruling settles doubtful cases.

levers.title: Know the country of origin — and where a hat gets it
levers.saves: The difference between country rates: +10% for Bangladesh, Cambodia or India, +12.5% for Vietnam, 10% in total for the EU, +37.5% for Chinese hats
levers.appliesTo: All lines; the gap is widest on caps and beanies from China
levers.document: Production records showing where the hat was made: for hats of 6501, 6502, 6504 and 6505 (except hair-nets), where it was wholly assembled — or, for a one-piece hat such as a knit-to-shape beanie, where it was knitted or the fabric was formed.
levers.caveat: Cutting in one country and sewing in another, or only embroidering, adding labels or packing, may not move the origin. The Section 301 and 338 duties follow the country of origin, and CBP can ask for proof.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 51, 52

levers.title: Claim USMCA on hats made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 9.4%, or a per-kilo-plus-percent rate) plus the 10% Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: All lines from Mexico; from Canada, all lines except 6505.00.60 and 6506.10.60
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, kept ready for CBP.
levers.caveat: The Chapter 65 rule is a change of heading: a cap cut and sewn in Mexico from imported fabric qualifies, but one assembled from imported crowns, visors or other 6507 parts does not, and hat bodies of 6501–6502 must come from outside the chapter. USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 6505.00.60 and 6506.10.60 from Canada. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS General Note 11 (USMCA rules of origin, Chapter 65)

levers.title: Claim CAFTA-DR, the Jordan FTA, AGOA or another FTA
levers.saves: The base rate; for CAFTA-DR hats from Guatemala or El Salvador and for all Jordanian hats, the Section 301 duty too
levers.appliesTo: Dutiable lines whose Special column lists the program: CAFTA-DR (P), Jordan (JO), AGOA (D, some lines only), Korea (KR), Colombia (CO), Peru (PE) and the other FTA partners
levers.document: The origin proof each program requires (a certification or declaration of origin, or the AGOA documentation) and records to back it up.
levers.caveat: An FTA removes the base rate but, except where a note 52(j) list says otherwise, not the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)). The note 52(j) lists for Guatemala, El Salvador and Jordan cover every Chapter 65 line except safety headgear. The CAFTA-DR textile exemption (note 52(i)) does not reach hats, because general note 29(d)(v) leaves headings 6501–6504 and hats of former 6505.90 out of "textile or apparel good" — so CAFTA-DR caps from Honduras, the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Costa Rica pay the Section 301 duty. GSP (A, A*) has been expired since December 31, 2020 and the Nepal program (NP) since December 31, 2025.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a), (i), (j)

levers.title: Use the China exclusions for disposable caps and some helmets
levers.saves: The 25% List 3 duty on nonwoven disposable caps, or the 7.5% List 4A duty on the excluded motorcycle and bicycle helmets
levers.appliesTo: 6505.00.80.15 (nonwoven disposable headgear without peaks or visors); 6506.10.60.30 (motorcycle helmets); bicycle helmets in 6506.10.60.45 with shells of PVC, polycarbonate or ABS and an inner liner of expanded polypropylene or polystyrene
levers.document: Product specifications showing the goods match the exclusion; report 9903.88.69 instead of 9903.88.03 or 9903.88.15.
levers.caveat: In effect through November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends them again. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.31) still applies.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 20(vvv)(iii)–(iv), 9903.88.69

levers.title: Value at the first sale for export when you buy through a middleman
levers.saves: Every ad valorem duty is charged on a lower value — the base rate and the 10%–50% extra duties included — when the factory price to a trading company or brand owner is lower than the price you pay
levers.appliesTo: All lines bought through a trading company, agent-buyer or brand owner rather than straight from the maker
levers.document: Proof that the first sale was a bona fide sale for export to the United States at arm's length: the factory invoice, contracts and payment records.
levers.caveat: Only a sale clearly destined for the U.S. qualifies, and the importer must be able to show the earlier price at entry.

levers.title: Assemble abroad from U.S.-made components (9802.00.80)
levers.saves: Duty — including the Section 301 duty — on the value of U.S.-made components, such as U.S.-cut cap panels or visors, sewn into hats abroad
levers.appliesTo: Caps and hats sewn abroad from components fabricated in the United States
levers.document: The assembler's declaration and the importer's endorsement that 19 CFR 10.24 requires, with records of the U.S. components.
levers.caveat: The components must be fabricated in the U.S., ready for assembly and not advanced in value abroad except by assembly. The Section 301 duty applies to the value of the hat less the U.S. components (U.S. note 52(a)); the hat's origin is still where it was assembled.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Recover duty on goods you export or destroy
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, when the imported goods (or goods made from them) are exported or destroyed
levers.appliesTo: Any line — for example caps re-exported to Canadian or Latin American customers
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import, manufacturing and export records.
levers.caveat: Claims have filing deadlines and record-keeping rules; check whether a given Chapter 99 duty is eligible before relying on it.

levers.title: Hold, decorate or relabel goods in a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: No duty on goods re-exported from the zone, and duty deferred until goods leave it for the U.S. market
levers.appliesTo: Any line — useful for blank caps stocked for several markets
levers.document: Zone admission (CBP Form 214) and the zone operator's inventory records.
levers.caveat: Goods entered for U.S. consumption from a zone pay the duties in force on the entry date. CPSC certificate eFiling for goods entered from a zone applies from January 8, 2027.

levers.title: Use a Chapter 98 provision for U.S. goods coming back
levers.saves: All duty on U.S.-made goods returned unchanged (9801.00.10), for example unsold caps sent back by a foreign distributor
levers.appliesTo: Any line, for American goods returned without having been advanced in value or improved abroad
levers.document: Proof of U.S. origin and of the export, as CBP requires for the provision.
levers.caveat: The Section 301 and 338 duties also do not apply to goods properly entered under Chapter 98, except subchapter XXIII and 9802.00.40–9802.00.80 (U.S. notes 51(a) and 52(a)).

levers.title: Get a binding classification ruling
levers.saves: Certainty where the line decides the rate and the extra duty: knitted versus woven, cotton versus man-made fiber, braid or not; a helmet of reinforced plastics (6506.10.30) or not (6506.10.60, on the Canada Section 338 list)
levers.appliesTo: Any line where the material, construction or use decides the line
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the article, its materials by weight, construction and use.
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a changed design or material may need a new one.

rules.title: Bicycle helmets must meet the CPSC safety standard and carry its certification label, which is the helmet's certificate of compliance; the importer counts as the manufacturer and must run a reasonable testing program. From July 8, 2026 the certificate data must be eFiled in ACE with the entry. Helmets for children 12 and under need third-party testing by a CPSC-accepted lab

Motorcycle helmets must meet FMVSS No. 218 and carry its labels, including the "DOT" certification label; at entry the importer files the HS-7 declaration that the equipment conforms, and a foreign manufacturer must name a U.S. agent for service

Textile headwear is wearing apparel under the Textile Act: label the fiber content by generic name and percentage, the country where it was made and the maker's name or RN. Hats are excluded from the care-labeling rule
Hats containing wool (wool beanies, wool-felt hats) are labeled under the Wool Products Labeling Act instead of the Textile Act
The clothing flammability standard does not apply to hats, unless the hat covers or forms part of a covering for the neck, face or shoulders (for example a balaclava)
Furskin headgear is a fur product: the label and invoice must give the animal name from the Fur Products Name Guide, the country of origin and whether the fur is dyed or pieced

Headgear of the fur of a wild species is a wildlife product: it must be declared on Form 3-177 and cleared by FWS before CBP releases it; furs of domesticated animals (rabbit, sheep and others listed in 50 CFR 14.4) are exempt
Country-of-origin marking in English, legible, indelible and permanent enough to reach the ultimate purchaser — on the hat or helmet itself or its retail container

Hats of headings 6501, 6502, 6504 and 6505 (except hair-nets) are "textile products": their origin is the country where they were wholly assembled or, for one-piece hats, where the fabric was formed or the hat was knitted

Report the Chapter 99 headings with the line: the 2026 Section 301 heading for the country (or its note 52(j) exemption), China List 3 (9903.88.03) or List 4A (9903.88.15) or their exclusion (9903.88.69), Brazil (9903.05.01), Canada Section 338 (9903.03.14)

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 30, 50–52

groups.label: Felt hat forms, hat bodies & hoods (not yet shaped)
groups.note: Unfinished felt hat bodies. No agency license. Their origin follows the textile rules of 19 CFR 102.21.

groups.label: Plaited hat shapes (straw and other strips, not yet shaped)
groups.note: Unfinished plaited hat shapes. No agency license. Shapes made by sewing (other than sewing strips in spirals) are not here (Chapter 65, note 2).

groups.label: Straw & other plaited hats
groups.note: No agency license for straw or plaited hats. Hats of man-made-fiber braid are textile products for the FTC labeling rules.

groups.label: Knitted & textile hats and caps, felt hats, hair-nets
groups.note: The FTC Textile and Wool Acts govern the labels on caps and beanies; the care-labeling rule and the clothing flammability standard do not apply to hats. Knitted man-made-fiber hats (6505.00.60) from Canada pay the 50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA.

groups.label: Helmets & safety headgear; rubber, plastic, fur & leather headgear
groups.note: Bicycle helmets (athletic lines 6506.10.30.45 and 6506.10.60.45) fall under CPSC's 16 CFR part 1203; motorcycle helmets (6506.10.30.30, 6506.10.60.30) under NHTSA's FMVSS 218. Hard hats have no federal entry rule; OSHA's head-protection standard (29 CFR 1910.135) tells employers which hard hats workers must wear. Safety headgear of 6506.10.60 from Canada pays the 50% Section 338 duty.

groups.label: Hat parts: headbands, linings, frames, peaks (visors), chin straps
groups.note: Hat parts — sweatbands, linings, frames, peaks and chin straps — are Free and need no agency license. A stand-alone headband worn as a hair accessory is not a part of headgear and is classified by its material elsewhere.

tariffEngineering.disclaimer: A checklist of where the rules are, with links to the regulations and the tariff schedule — not legal advice. Which line a hat or helmet falls in, where it originates and which Chapter 99 duties apply depend on the facts of each shipment, and the extra duties change by Federal Register notice and CBP guidance; confirm the current headings and the CPSC and NHTSA requirements before each shipment.

seo.title: Hat, Cap & Helmet Tariff FAQ: China, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Mexico, HS Codes for Caps, Beanies & Helmets (HTS Ch. 65) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. tariffs on headgear: tariffs on hats from China, Vietnam, Bangladesh and Mexico, the HS codes for baseball caps, beanies, bucket, straw, felt and cowboy hats, hair-nets and visors, and the duty and rules for motorcycle, bicycle, hockey and safety helmets.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about U.S. tariffs and import rules for hats, caps and helmets. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: 49 of the 64 Chapter 65 lines carry a base duty, mostly 6%–9.4% or a per-kilo charge plus a percentage: 7.5% for a woven cotton cap, 18.7¢/kg + 6.8% for a polyester cap, 20¢/kg + 7% for an acrylic beanie. Helmets, hard hats, fur-felt hats and hat parts are Free.

Since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 duty is added by country: +12.5% for Vietnam and Thailand, +10% for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and India, and 10% in total for the EU and Taiwan. Myanmar, Laos and Haiti are outside the 60 economies.

China pays the most: +12.5% plus 25% (List 3) on hats and caps — 45% on a cotton cap — and +12.5% plus 7.5% (List 4A) on helmets and hair-nets; exclusions for disposable caps and some motorcycle and bicycle helmets run to November 9, 2026.

USMCA-qualifying hats from Mexico pay nothing; the Chapter 65 USMCA rule is a change of heading, so caps sewn in Mexico from imported fabric can qualify. From Canada, knitted synthetic hats (6505.00.60) and most helmets (6506.10.60) pay 50% Section 338 even under USMCA.

The IEEPA duties (up to 177.5% on Chinese cotton caps in spring 2025, 20% on Vietnam and Bangladesh from August 2025) ended February 24, 2026; the 10% Section 122 surcharge ended July 23, 2026. De minimis remains suspended, so low-value hat parcels pay duty.

Bicycle helmets need CPSC certification under 16 CFR part 1203 (certificate data eFiled at entry since July 8, 2026); motorcycle helmets need the FMVSS 218 "DOT" label and an HS-7 declaration; textile hats need FTC fiber, origin and maker labels.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on hats imported into the U.S.?
faqs.answer: Yes. The base rate depends on the material: a woven cotton cap pays 7.5%, a knitted cotton hat 7.9%, a polyester cap 18.7¢/kg + 6.8%, an acrylic beanie 20¢/kg + 7%, a sewn straw hat 6%, a fur-felt hat Free. Since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 duty is added by country: Vietnam +12.5%, Bangladesh, Cambodia and Indonesia +10%, the EU 10% in total, China +37.5%. USMCA-qualifying hats from Mexico pay nothing. And with de minimis suspended, even a single hat shipped from abroad pays duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code (tariff code) for hats?
faqs.answer: Hats are in HS Chapter 65. Most finished hats and caps are 6505.00 (knitted, or made up from textile fabric or felt; also hair-nets); hats plaited or made of strips, such as straw hats, are 6504.00; helmets and other safety headgear 6506.10; rubber, plastic, fur and leather headgear 6506.91 and 6506.99; hat parts 6507.00. The 10-digit U.S. number then depends on fiber, knitted or woven construction and, for many lines, whether the hat is for babies or is a visor.

faqs.question: What is the HTS code and tariff for a baseball cap?
faqs.answer: A woven cotton baseball cap is 6505.00.20.60 (7.5%); knitted cotton 6505.00.15.40 (7.9%); woven polyester or nylon 6505.00.80.90 (18.7¢/kg + 6.8%); knitted man-made fibers 6505.00.60.90 (20¢/kg + 7%). Add the country duty: a cotton cap pays 20% from Vietnam, 17.5% from Bangladesh, 45% from China, nothing from Mexico under USMCA.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a beanie or knit hat?
faqs.answer: Knitted hats are classified by fiber: acrylic or polyester 6505.00.60.90 (20¢/kg + 7%; 6505.00.60.40 if 23% or more wool), wool 6505.00.30.90 (25.4¢/kg + 7.7%), cotton 6505.00.15.40 (7.9%). A Chinese acrylic beanie pays about 45% in all; from Canada, 6505.00.60 carries the 50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a bucket hat or a straw hat?
searchedAs: hs code for cotton bucket hat
faqs.answer: A woven cotton bucket hat is 6505.00.20.60 (7.5%); polyester or nylon 6505.00.80.90 (18.7¢/kg + 6.8%). Straw hats plaited of vegetable fiber or paper yarn are 6504.00.30 if sewn (6%) or 6504.00.60 if not (94¢/doz. + 4.6%); hats of plastic braid or other strips 6504.00.90 (6.8%). Unfinished straw hat shapes are heading 6502.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a felt or cowboy hat?
faqs.answer: Felt hats made from felt hat bodies are 6505.00.04 if of fur felt (Free) or 6505.00.08.00 if of wool or other felt (13.5¢/kg + 6.3% + 1.9¢ each). A straw cowboy hat is classified as a plaited hat of 6504. Unblocked felt hat bodies are 6501. An Italian fur-felt fedora pays 10% in total since July 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on hats and caps from China?
searchedAs: us tariffs on clothing from china
current tariffs on clothing from china
faqs.answer: Chinese hats and caps pay the base rate plus 12.5% (2026 Section 301, 9903.05.31) plus 25% (List 3, 9903.88.03): 45% on a cotton cap, 18.7¢/kg + 44.3% on a polyester cap, 20¢/kg + 44.5% on an acrylic beanie. Helmets and hair-nets pay 12.5% plus 7.5% (List 4A) instead. Nonwoven disposable caps, motorcycle helmets of 6506.10.60.30 and some bicycle helmets skip the List 3 or 4A duty through November 9, 2026. China supplied $874M of headgear in 2025, 24.0% less than in 2024.

faqs.question: What are the U.S. tariffs on hats from Vietnam and Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Since July 24, 2026 Vietnamese goods pay the base rate plus 12.5% Section 301 (9903.05.84) — 20% on a cotton cap — and Bangladeshi goods plus 10% (9903.05.26) — 17.5% on a cotton cap. No Chapter 65 line is exempt for either country. The 20% IEEPA reciprocal tariffs on both (August 7, 2025 to February 24, 2026) have ended. Vietnam supplied $608M of headgear in 2025 and Bangladesh $389M.

faqs.question: Do hats made in Mexico pay U.S. tariffs?
faqs.answer: Not if they qualify under USMCA: the claim removes both the base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.94). The Chapter 65 rule of origin is a change of heading, so a cap cut and sewn in Mexico from imported fabric, or a straw hat plaited there, can qualify; one assembled from imported crowns or visors (heading 6507) does not. Non-qualifying Mexican hats pay the base rate plus 10%. Mexico supplied $471M in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for safety helmets and hard hats?
faqs.answer: Safety headgear is 6506.10: 6506.10.30 if of reinforced or laminated plastics, 6506.10.60 otherwise, with suffix .30 for motorcycle helmets, .45 for athletic and sporting helmets and .75 for other safety headgear such as hard hats. All are Free; the extra duty is +12.5% from Vietnam, 10% in total from Taiwan, 20% from China. Hard hats need no federal entry document; OSHA's 29 CFR 1910.135 sets which hard hats employers must provide.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for motorcycle helmets, and what rules apply?
faqs.answer: Motorcycle helmets are 6506.10.30.30 (reinforced or laminated plastics) or 6506.10.60.30 (other), both Free. From China they pay 20%, or 12.5% for 6506.10.60.30 while its List 4A exclusion runs (to November 9, 2026). Every motorcycle helmet must meet FMVSS 218 (49 CFR 571.218) and carry the "DOT" certification label, and the importer declares conformity on NHTSA's HS-7 form at entry (49 CFR 591.5).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a bicycle helmet, and what does CPSC require?
faqs.answer: Bicycle helmets are athletic headgear: 6506.10.60.45, or 6506.10.30.45 if of reinforced or laminated plastics — Free. They must meet the CPSC standard in 16 CFR part 1203 and carry its certification label; the importer must test them, and since July 8, 2026 must eFile the certificate data with the entry. From China they pay 20%, or 12.5% if they match the exclusion for PVC, polycarbonate or ABS shells with EPS or EPP liners.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for hockey and ski helmets?
faqs.answer: Hockey, ski and other sports helmets are athletic headgear of 6506.10.30.45 or 6506.10.60.45, Free. From Canada, 6506.10.60 is on the Section 338 list: a USMCA-qualifying Canadian hockey helmet of 6506.10.60 pays 50%, a non-qualifying one 60%; one of reinforced or laminated plastics (6506.10.30) is not on the list. From the EU or Taiwan they pay 10% in total, from China 20%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a hair net?
searchedAs: hs tariff code for hair net
faqs.answer: Hair-nets of any material are 6505.00.01.00, 9.4%. From China they pay 29.4% (List 4A + 12.5%). Nonwoven disposable caps without peaks (bouffant caps) are 6505.00.80.15 (18.7¢/kg + 6.8%), excluded from China's List 3 duty through November 9, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a sun visor, helmet visor or headband?
faqs.answer: A sun visor — headgear that leaves the crown uncovered — has its own "visor" suffix within each 6505 fiber line (for example 6505.00.80.50 for woven man-made fibers, 6505.00.15.25 for knitted cotton); plastic visors are 6506.91.00.45 (Free). Peaks (visors), chin straps, sweatbands and linings made as parts of headgear are 6507.00.00 (Free). A headband worn on its own is not Chapter 65 headgear and is classified by its material.
